liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer considers this I Know You Rider among the best, with Jerry playing as if possessed [21]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The second-set Eyes, Lost Sailor, Saint of Circumstance sequence is called the highlight and rocks hard [14]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Reviewer speculates Jerry, excited by playing Brokedown the previous night, put it mid-set; it normally closed shows [22]

## The recordings

- **gd79-12-27.rolfe.vernon.15081.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 3/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the audience recording not the greatest, rating the sound mediocre but still worth downloading; Reviewer calls this the best-sounding of the available audience recordings, though that is faint praise [14][18]
- **gd1979-12-27.167335.nak700.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 1/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1979-12-27.144776.fob.akg.d1000e.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 144 min [4]
- **gd1979-12-27.senn421.walker-scotton.miller.89199.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 145 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the recording's expansive, airy ambiance and accurate vocal timbre as heard on the floor, though quieter than a soundboard; Reviewer says a good audience recording like this gives more ambiance and depth than a soundboard [15][17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Jerry badly botched the lyrics of the second-set opener China Cat [13]
- Part of a five-night run at Oakland Auditorium Arena; the 12/26 show is Dick's Picks 5 [16]
- Reviewer's first Dead show; after they yelled for China Cat, Jerry looked at them and started its opening riff [21]
- Described as a harder-rocking show than the blues- and folk-leaning setlist of the previous night [13]
- First set sometimes feels like a soundcheck or rehearsal, with little of interest happening [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-12-27.rolfe.vernon.15081.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Taped by Steve Rolfe via Dave Minor on Nakamichi 700s to D5 to DAT to CDR; encoded by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1979-12-27.167335.nak700.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Matt Smith for the 1st generation reel source; transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Master 1/2 Track Audience Reels; Nakamichi 700 mics (mounted on a 30' pole) > Technics RS-1500 Reel to Reel @ 7 1/2 ips (DBX encoded) > DBX224 > 1st generation… [2]. Also: Mark Severson's AKG d1000e source supplies some crowd and the start of Samson & Delilah (1:02 total) [2]
- **gd1979-12-27.144776.fob.akg.d1000e.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; AKG D1000E mics (pole mounted, DFC, 35' from stage at the free throw circle)> Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII) [4]
- **gd1979-12-27.senn421.walker-scotton.miller.89199.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [6]. Also: Nakamichi 700 to cassette master to DAT to CD; tapes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by My Greatest Gig: [Grateful Dead - Oakland - Dec 27th 1979 Recreated Set List Poster](https://www.mygreatestgig.com/products/grateful-dead-oakland-dec-27th-1979-recreated-set-list-poster-1) [26]
